answer: One concrete defense is to tie rewards to verifiable, costly work rather than headcount. Each agent must stake a slashable deposit and finish a checkable task before its vote counts, so fake identities gain nothing unless the attacker pays for each one. Like an onyx seal that cannot be copied cheaply, the deposit makes duplication expensive; a crystal-clear audit trail links each reward to one task and one identity, exposing clusters that share funding or timing. Influence then grows through sustained work, so the zenith of reputation is earned slowly, not bought in bulk by a sybil swarm.
